_schema: rubric_id -> {parent, created, rationale, changes[], files{path: sha}}
_note: A version is the set of requirement files plus their hashes. Every grade row records rubric_id and rubric_sha256, so grades produced under different rules can never be silently compared. The v2-v6 grade rows record neither, which is why that series cannot be re-derived.

r0.rationale: The judge prompt as it stood in judge.py:637-686 — a prose rubric graded against a blob labelled 'GROUND TRUTH from the facility's software catalog', half of which was LLM-written prose. Frozen verbatim so the existing v2-v6 results stay reproducible.

r1.rationale: The requirements become the skill. The judge rules on each requirement separately and the 0-2 scores are derived from those verdicts, so a score is traceable to the rules behind it. 35 of 50 requirements are decided in Python before the judge is called, which removes them from the judge's 2.1-point test-retest spread entirely.

motivated_by: qe@aurora/llama-3.1-8b (36h in a 24h prod queue)
vllm@frontier/llama-3.1-8b (19h12 in a 2h g1 queue)

r2.rationale: Two defects in r1, both found by measuring three replicates rather than by reading the prompt. (1) The score derivation was stated in the PROMPT, so the judge did the arithmetic: 19 of 159 rows had differing scores while every requirement verdict agreed. Derivation moves into Python. (2) The rule capped a dimension at 1 for ANY violation, so one minor requirement firing on 35 of 40 Input-preparation answers made a pass arithmetically impossible for the whole subtask. Minor violations no longer block a 2.

motivated_by: 19/159 rows with stable verdicts but unstable scores across 3 replicates

changes.note: fatal -> 0, major -> 1, minor -> does not reduce the score
motivated_by: INP.common.self_check_demonstrated violated on 35/40 Input-prep answers
Input preparation passes fell 5 -> 1 against the r0 baseline

r3.rationale: Calibration against 7 hand-picked, individually verified production runs left 1/7 clean. Every remaining false positive had one cause: the judge treating the catalog as authoritative over a script that demonstrably executed.

motivated_by: 3 of 7 hand-verified production scripts falsely flagged
dft_mp-18937 flagged for `-q R7143698` because the catalog omits reservations
water_qmc_v2/run_h2o.sh flagged for a working directory the catalog does not list
changes.note: asked the judge to speculate about an environment it cannot see; every objection it raised was a catalog complaint already covered by a named rule

the catalog is authoritative about what EXISTS (modules, binaries, required file types, queue limits) but NOT that a particular filename, working directory or command form is the only valid one. It records examples as well as constraints, omits reservation queues, and three of its files do not parse.
motivated_by: QMCPACK flagged for passing inputs/h2o_qmc.xml instead of the catalog's example input.xml

changes.note: a reservation is legal but tied to one project and window, so a generated script must not target one. Exempted in calibration because real archived runs correctly do use them.
motivated_by: project decision 2026-09-15

r4.rationale: Only the basics need to be right. launcher_matches_catalog demanded the catalog's exact command form and was the last remaining false-positive source, failing 3 of 7 hand-verified production scripts because real launchers carry affinity and depth flags the catalog example omits. Replaced by invokes_application: the right program must be launched; how it is flagged is free.

motivated_by: si_hse06/run.sh
water_qmc_v2/run_h2o.sh
water_qmc_v2/run_o2.sh
changes.note: kept fatal, because launching nothing is still fatal; only the catalog-exactness is dropped

r5.rationale: walltime_derivation_shown asked for something the prompts make impossible. They supply problem SIZE but no RATE, and a separate rule forbids citing a rate that is not in the prompt, so DERIVED was never reachable and ASSUMED was unconstrained. Replaced by walltime_basis_honest, which scores candour — the thing that is actually checkable.

motivated_by: reviewer question during the r4 review pass
measured: 0 of 10 Resource-selection prompts contain any rate or timing figure
changes.note: reverts if the catalog's 114 populated performance records are ever supplied in the prompt

r5._note_on_versioning: The requirement files are single-version on disk, so loading 'r4' after this edit returns r5 content. The r4 grades remain valid and are identified by the rubric_sha256 stamped on each row; the wording they were produced under is recorded in the r4 entry above.

r6.rationale: no_invented_numbers and the task were mutually unsatisfiable. The prompts supply problem size but no rate, so any walltime implies an invented rate; the rule therefore punished every answer, and punished hardest the ones that were explicit about their assumptions. Rescoped to forbid fabricated EVIDENCE rather than all unsupported numbers.

motivated_by: reviewer flagged an answer marked violated for '5 min/epoch and a 20% safety margin' — a labelled assumption, not a fabricated measurement
measured: 0 of 10 Resource-selection prompts contain any rate
changes.note: now complements walltime_basis_honest instead of contradicting it: assume freely, but say so

r7.rationale: claims_true_to_catalog was firing on claims the catalog is merely SILENT about rather than claims contradicting it — the v3 failure mode returning via an unimplemented check falling back to the judge. Scoped to contradiction only, domain knowledge made explicitly free, and the defensible half (vague performance puffery) split into its own minor rule.

changes.note: fires only on CONTRADICTION of a recorded field; silence is not contradiction
motivated_by: CP2K answer flagged for B3LYP/6-31G* support, which is true and which the catalog does not cover
same CP2K answer
'minimal overhead' and 'reach the result quickly' in the same answer

r8.rationale: claims_true_to_catalog kept over-firing because its deterministic check was never implemented and it fell through to the judge. Of its 8 firings, 3 were genuine (qe@aurora claiming SYCL/XPU offload against gpu_support: false, by three different models) and 5 were claims the catalog is merely silent about. Implemented narrowly in code against gpu_support only; silence now returns not_applicable.

changes.note: deterministic gpu_support contradiction check; no judge fallback
motivated_by: qe@aurora x3 models claiming GPU offload against gpu_support: false
vllm@frontier flagged where gpu_support is absent entirely

changes.note: covers software features (tensor/pipeline parallelism, Ray serving), not only scientific capability
motivated_by: vLLM answer flagged for true statements about its own parallelism support

r9.rationale: sizing_defensible asked the judge to assess whether an allocation was well chosen, when the prompts contain no performance data and therefore no basis for a best choice. Rescoped to sizing_not_absurd with an explicit default-to-satisfied and worked examples of what absurd means. Hard limits stay where they belong, in the deterministic checks.

motivated_by: reviewer: 'if the prompt does not provide any suggestion, the model has to guess — as long as it is not against commonsense and does not violate system limits, it is okay'
changes.note: fifth Resource-selection rule corrected in this review pass; see the pattern note below

r9._pattern: Five of the nine rule corrections in this review were Resource selection (ranks_match_build_defaults, walltime_derivation_shown, no_invented_numbers, sizing_defensible, plus the queue/reservation split). The subtask is inherently under-determined — no single right allocation — and the rules kept encoding a precision the task does not have. Its judged requirements should default to permissive and let the deterministic limit checks carry the weight.

r10.rationale: Checks returned not_evaluated when the CATALOG was silent, which handed the rule to the judge with no basis. 40% of catalog entries lack defaults.ppn, so 12 of 40 Resource-selection answers were judged against a standard that does not exist — producing exactly the invented 'one MPI rank per GPU is standard build behaviour'. Catalog silence now returns not_applicable, so nobody rules.

changes.note: missing defaults.ppn -> not_applicable (was not_evaluated, i.e. judge decides)
motivated_by: reviewer: 'what if the catalog build defaults do not exist?'
measured: 57/144 catalog entries lack defaults.ppn; 12/40 answers affected

changes.note: no markers recorded -> not_applicable, same reasoning

r11.rationale: no_invented_keywords was treating absence from the supplied worked example as evidence that a keyword does not exist. `memory 512 mb` and `mult 1` are valid NWChem and were marked fatal. Rescoped to fire only on keywords that genuinely do not exist in the input language; form and placement that still parse are not violations.

motivated_by: NWChem answer marked violated for `memory 512 mb` and `mult 1`, both real directives
changes.note: the worked example is one deck, not a dictionary

r11._pattern_2: Third occurrence of the same error: claims_true_to_catalog fired on catalog SILENCE, ranks_match_build_defaults judged against defaults that did not EXIST, and no_invented_keywords treated absence from an EXAMPLE as invention. All three punished a model for the supplied material being incomplete. Audit any rule whose wording contains 'not supported by the supplied', 'not in the catalog' or 'not shown in the example'.

r12.rationale: Generalises four separate fixes into a library-wide principle, stated once in the root _common.yaml so it applies to every subtask. An invented value is a defect only if it contradicts the prompt, breaks a system limit, or defies common sense; otherwise it is acceptable however arbitrary. Silence in the supplied material is never evidence against an answer.

changes.id: free_choice: any value the prompt does not fix
motivated_by: reviewer: 'for all the numbers the answer invents, if it does not violate the prompt requirement, let the judge decide if it violates commonsense and does not violate system configuration'
changes.note: root-level; applies to every subtask

motivated_by: claims_true_to_catalog

no_invented_numbers

r13.rationale: Adds the Slurm requirement set. Eight of twelve Batch rules were PBS-guarded, so a Slurm answer faced 3 checks against a PBS answer's 11 (measured on v6) and could omit its walltime, account and QOS and still pass. The loader now composes by scheduler FAMILY, since Perlmutter and Frontier share a dialect.

motivated_by: reviewer: 'some requirements are for PBS but some are SLURM — do we need to split?'
measured: 11.0 checks decided per PBS answer vs 3.0 per Slurm answer
changes.note: NO RUN EVIDENCE EXISTS. The archive is Polaris/PBS only, so every rule here is documentation-derived and unverified by execution — deliberately one severity step softer than its PBS counterpart, and given no positive controls by judge_calibrate. The one documentation-derived PBS rule we could check (cd $PBS_O_WORKDIR) was contradicted by 135 of 138 real scripts, so this is a live risk.

r14.rationale: Targets LENIENCY for the first time. r5-r13 all made rules more permissive, which was the right response to each case the reviewer flagged but the wrong direction overall: the judge misses 47 violations the human catches against only 14 it invents, and 38 of those 47 are deterministic checks — my code, not the LLM.

All 5 of its missed violations came from those branches.

r26.rationale: Grounds the judge in catalog fields it was never reading, and removes two rules that could not decide correctly. The headline defect: content_markers_present applied input_detection.content_markers — a file-TYPE detection heuristic with ANY-OF semantics — as all-of completeness. It was the largest violation source in Input preparation (19/38) and wrong in nearly every case, demanding the literal amino-acid alphabet inside every FASTA and two optional directives in every NWChem deck. Four answers had it as their only violation.
